Real run-to-run non-determinism confirmed via 4 independent re-runs (identical seed/code): event_count varied 10/11/11/10, score varied -0.272/-0.300/-0.249/-0.272. Watchdog trips confirmed present in every run (kernel.py's tick-budget throttle, D06 F6), starting tick ~25. 5 other FAST-tier scenarios sampled the same way (dungeon_crawl_seed42_500t, highland_traverse_seed42_200t, hero_guild_routing_seed42_500t, simq_routing_test_seed123_500t, simq_routing_test_seed456_500t) were stable or showed only sub-tolerance noise despite the same watchdog trips firing -- this scenario's own low PROGRESSION event count (10-11) makes it unusually sensitive to which individual events the throttle happens to drop, unlike scenarios with a larger event sample. Not a code defect; a real, low-event-count sample-size sensitivity to an already-documented engine mechanism.
